samples.summary: 'should write a single-cell paste through the merge anchor' does not exercise the new `normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell)` line it appears to cover
samples.evidence: The test does `sheet.selectStart({ r: 1, c: 2 })` before pasting, but `selectStart` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3642) already does `this.setActiveCell(this.normalizeRefToAnchor(ref))`, so `activeCell` is A1 before `paste` runs. The new `const target = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell)` at sheet.ts:2194 is therefore a no-op in this test and the assertions (A1/B1 == '99') would hold with the old `this.activeCell` code too. The test does meaningfully cover the single-cell `isSameRef(destRange[0], destRange[1])` exemption, but nothing in the suite covers the anchor-normalization of a non-normalized active cell (e.g. an activeCell set through a path that does not normalize).

samples.summary: No test covers the new refusal when a copied merged block is only partially inside the copied source range
samples.evidence: paste() returns early when `copiedMerges.some((m) => !isRangeInRange(m.range, sourceRange))`. None of the 12 new tests copies a range that only partially overlaps a merge; every test copies either the exact merged block or a range with no merge. Note `copy()` uses `getRangeOrActiveCell()` which calls `expandRangeToMergedBoundaries` (sheet.ts:3180), so this branch may be unreachable — either way it ships with zero coverage (and if unreachable that is a correctness/dead-code concern for another lens).

samples.summary: The cut-anchor exemption (`!cutAnchors.has(m.anchorSref)`) for a cut-paste whose destination overlaps its own source is untested
samples.evidence: The new filter exempts merges inside the cut source from the destination split-refusal, so an overlapping cut-paste (e.g. cut A1:B1 merged, paste at B1) is not refused. All cut tests in the new describe block paste to a disjoint destination (row 3 vs row 1), so the overlap path — the only reason the exemption exists — never executes.
searchedFor: read all new cut tests in merge.test.ts (lines 128-215)

samples.summary: Merge deletion is only asserted against the in-memory `this.merges` cache, never against the store
samples.evidence: 'should persist the propagated merge to the store' (line 108) checks `store.getMerges()` for the added merge, but the drop paths (`await this.store.deleteMerge(...)` at sheet.ts:2337, used by the overwrite and cut cases) are only verified via `sheet.getMerges()` (lines 164, 140), which reads the in-memory map updated on the adjacent line. A store-level deleteMerge failure/omission would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The spill-handling branches of the extracted `clearCellsUnderMerge` have no test on either the paste or the move path
samples.evidence: clearCellsUnderMerge contains spillAnchor skip, spill-anchor ghost cleanup and spillBlocked handling, and is now invoked from the new paste merge propagation (sheet.ts:2343). `grep -i spill packages/sheets/test` returns no hits in merge.test.ts (only calculation/data-validation/formatting/style-mutation/formula tests), so no test places a spill anchor or ghost under a merge being created by paste or move — the extraction could silently drop these branches without any test failing.

samples.summary: The HTML paste branch (html2grid with the anchor-normalized target) has no test
samples.evidence: `grep 'isSpreadsheetHtml|paste({ html|html:' packages/sheets/test` matches only packages/sheets/test/model/grids.test.ts; no Sheet-level test pastes HTML, so the changed `html2grid(html, target)` call and merge interaction on that branch are uncovered. The plain-TSV tests cover the equivalent generic logic, hence nit.

samples.summary: All new merge copy-paste tests use a single 1x2 merged block; multi-row spans and multiple blocks in one copied range are untested
samples.evidence: Every test in the new 'Sheet merge + copy-paste' describe merges exactly one 1-row x 2-col block. `pastedMerges` is a list and `mergeCoveredSrefs` iterates rows and cols, but no test copies a range containing two merged blocks or a block spanning >1 row, so row-delta translation and multi-block propagation are unexercised.
